relevance_note: This single-centre cohort of 79 monogenic autoinflammatory disease patients includes one Majeed syndrome patient described individually: "Our case was a male patient who developed fever and bone pain soon after birth" with "c.2327+1G>C and c.1691_1694delGAGA of LPIN2".
method_note: Read by hand; a short script only assembled the JSON and checked spans. Only one in-scope person (the Majeed syndrome patient, Table 2 row 'Majeed syndrome (n = 1)' and the Results paragraph); all other cohort members carry variants in other genes and get no rows. Label: the paper gives no label ('Our case' is a role word) and this is a cohort, not a case report, so rule 6 'unnamed person 1' was used; the Table 2 row is a disease-group row (n = 1), not a patient row, so rule 3 was not applied. Table 2 'Age onset (median, range)' gives 0.2 for this row with no unit stated, so onset was taken from the text ('soon after birth') and no ISO value was given. Zygosity is not stated (two LPIN2 variants found, but the paper does not say compound heterozygous or give phase/parental testing), so it is 'not reported'. Consanguinity 'no' comes from the Methods statement about all children in the study ('There was no consanguinity in these children.'). Ethnicity 'Chinese' comes from the study-wide description of the patients. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the only prior-report statement ('which have been analyzed and reported previously (12)') concerns NLRP12 variants/patients, not the Majeed patient, and speaks of variants rather than patients. Checklist: the paper says 'chronic osteomyelitis' and 'fever' without stating recurrent or multifocal, so 'chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis' and 'recurrent fever' were left 'not reported' (phenotypic_features rows record osteomyelitis and fever as observed); 'dermatosis'/'skin disorders' is not specified as neutrophilic, so 'neutrophilic dermatosis (Sweet syndrome)' is 'not reported'; 'highly elevated acute phase reactants' was taken as observed for 'elevated inflammatory markers (ESR/CRP)'. The study's inclusion criterion of elevated inflammation indices was not used as evidence. The Introduction-to-Majeed sentence about the 'classic triad' in early reports is background, not about this patient. Pathogenicity of c.1691_1694delGAGA: the paper says only that it 'has not been reported elsewhere', which is novelty, not a classification, so 'not reported'. No contradictions found.
